title: Rafi's Wiggling Seeds
markdown:
Sun popped! Sky bright pink and orange! Rafi bounced. Science club day! He dashed to the kitchen. Plum the rabbit twitched. Mr. Reed hummed. Breakfast smells!

"Morning!" Rafi chirped. "We plant seeds! Help them grow!"

Mr. Reed brought a big, clear jar. "Special seeds, Rafi," he rumbled. "Tiny promises. We'll help them wake up!"

Rafi beamed. He took a pinch of seeds. Tiny pebbles. He put a few on soil in the jar. Plum nudged more with her nose. They peered in. Sleeping seeds. Brown specks. Rafi poked the soil. "Awake yet?" he whispered. No sprout.

Plum tilted her head. "Sleepy, Rafi," she fluttered. "Like a nap."

Rafi frowned. He wanted sprouts now! He watched Mr. Reed water a plant. He saw a sunbeam splash. "Hmm," Rafi murmured. "Seeds need water? And sunshine for energy?"

He picked up the seed jar. He added a tiny dribble of water. Then, with determined hands, he placed the jar where the sunbeam danced. He and Plum sat, eyes glued. Suddenly, he saw it! A tiny movement! A seed gave a little shimmy. Then another!

"Plum! Look!" Rafi exclaimed, bursting with excitement. "They're wiggling!"

Plum's whiskers twitched. "They are!" she squeaked, doing a happy jump.

A little green tip poked out! Pushing through the soil! Another followed! Tiny worms stretching awake. Rafi clapped. A big grin spread. "They're waking up! The seeds are waking up!"

"Ah, but here's the thing," Mr. Reed rumbled. "Seeds need a drink, like your cereal. And they need sunshine for energy, like you need sunshine to play! It's science!"

Rafi nodded, gazing at the tiny green sprouts. He understood! It wasn't magic. It was science! A powerful feeling bubbled up. "We did it!" he declared, bouncing. "We helped them grow!"

Plum twitched her nose. "They look happy now!"

"And tomorrow," Rafi announced, his eyes shining, "we'll see BIGGER sprouts! And maybe tiny leaves!" He took a deep breath. "Today," Rafi declared, his voice full of promise, "is going to be AMAZING!"
characters: Rafi the question asker, Plum the rabbit, Mr. Reed
